narrative.overview:
The site is set like the front page of a newspaper, with one person as the whole edition. A masthead carries the name at poster scale, and tiers of articles below it zig-zag the way a broadsheet does: the wide column swaps sides each tier. Every article is a picture rather than a block of text: a globe, a circuit board, a fractal. Clicking one grows it to fill the screen at its own address, and the newspaper's grid lines stretch out to the edges of the viewport around it. Esc folds it back into the page.

The material is newsprint in negative. It's one tone in four values, with hairline dashed rules instead of boxes, no radii and no shadows. The only real colours are the work itself: the globe's violet network hubs and the fractals' matplotlib palettes. Light mode isn't a settings toggle. You reach it by bending the globe past halfway, and it then holds across visits. Motion is mechanical rather than soft: hover rings switch on in hard steps like a fluorescent tube, labels type themselves in, and an optional synthesized sound layer clicks and hums.
keyCharacteristics: Newspaper grid: masthead, tiers, dashed column rules, figure captions ("Fig. 1"), and a mono kicker over every headline.
Headlines are fitted to their box in container units (`cqw`), so each word fills its column.
Monochrome chrome: colour belongs only to the artwork.
Live art everywhere: WebGL and animated ASCII fields stand in for photos.
Hard-step motion and typed labels; reduced-motion collapses all of it.

rules.name: The Colour Is the Work Rule
rules.body: UI chrome never takes a hue. Colour on screen should always come from an artwork.

rules.name: The Two Ends Rule
rules.body: A theme is the same four tokens swapped. Never add a light-only or dark-only token for chrome.

rules.name: The Titles-Only Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif is too tall to read in. It sets names and titles only, never a sentence of body text.

rules.name: The Fitted Headline Rule
rules.body: Size headlines with `fillSize()` against the nearest `.fit` container. Never pick a fixed px size per word.

rules.name: The Flat Newsprint Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. Separation comes from a hairline or from space.

dos: Do keep every label in Plex Mono 300 at 10px, uppercase with 0.18em tracking, starting with a slash ("/About", "/Contact").
Do draw structure with 1px dashed `rule` hairlines; the outer page edges are the only solid rules.
Do let artwork carry all of the colour: the globe's violet and the fractal palettes.
Do give every opening thing both a click and a keyboard path, plus a visible focus state (the flicker ring).
Do use hard-step (`step-end`) timing for state changes that should feel electrical, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't round a corner or add a shadow.
Don't set body copy in Instrument Serif.
Don't add a UI accent colour. A hover is bone or dim, never a hue.
Don't fade a hover ring in smoothly; it catches like a tube.
